authority.workerRule: Workers never edit this ledger. Before assignment, the integration owner must set one assignee and exact non-overlapping ownedPaths for one item.
authority.completionRule: Only the integration owner may set complete after independent verification against the declared evidence identity.
authority.selectionRule: Only the integration owner may publish or change canonical selection state.

assignmentPolicy.canonicalOwnerRule: canonical owner-only roots/files can be read by a worker and emitted as a private content-bound proposal, but can never be a generated mutable candidate, active owned path, worker commit path, or tracked worker artifact; on an ordinary worker row they may appear in candidatePaths/supportPaths only when the exact path is also ownershipPlanning.readOnlyPaths and is therefore excluded from ownedPaths; a row without ownershipPlanning cannot list one; only an integration-owner transition may write them
assignmentPolicy.ownershipPathIdentityRule: authorization is ordinal case-sensitive over canonical forward-slash repository-relative literal paths; case folding is used only to reject collisions and never to grant ownership. Pre/post HEAD, index, worktree, and ignored inventories and every committed delta are collected with rename detection disabled. Both endpoints of any independently observed rename must be authorized, every base path that vanishes requires exact authorizedDeletion coverage, and a case-only rename, path alias, restored unowned path, or semantically inferred rename fails closed
assignmentPolicy.canonicalJsonDigestRule: recursively sort every object key by ordinal Unicode code point, retain array order exactly, encode ensure-ASCII compact JSON with comma/colon separators as UTF-8 without BOM, append exactly one LF, and take lowercase SHA-256

digestReferencePolicy.pathRule: one canonical portable repository/workspace-relative literal path with no machine prefix, traversal, wildcard, reparse alias, or case-fold duplicate
digestReferencePolicy.hashRule: sha256 is the lowercase raw-byte SHA-256 of the exact file at path
digestReferencePolicy.verificationRule: every non-null receiptFields value is exactly requiredKeys, is re-read from path, matches raw SHA-256, validates its named exact-key schema and cross-identities, and is retained until owner acceptance; a naked hash, untyped object, missing/unreadable path, wrong bytes, or extra key fails closed

ledgerSchemaPolicy.conditionalRule: ownershipPlanning is present only on policy-mapped worker rows and has exactly requiredOwnershipPlanningKeys; non-null authorizedDeletion has exactly requiredAuthorizedDeletionKeys; dispositionEvidence is an exact-key array; envelopeCompletion is present only on closure-envelope rows and is null or exact feature policy keys; generatedLane is present only on accepted-plan children; completionReceipt is present only on complete/accepted rows and has exact completion policy keys; completionEvidence and every unknown or misplaced key are forbidden
ledgerSchemaPolicy.unknownKeyRule: every object governed by an exact required/optional key list rejects extra, missing, duplicate-after-parse, case-variant, or inherited/defaulted keys before any state transition

assignmentAuthoritySlicePolicy.sourceClosureRule: selectedEvidenceSources is the exact ID-sorted transitive closure of the assigned row's sourceEvidence IDs through inputEvidence IDs; trackedAuthorityBlobs additionally includes only the top-level evidenceSources[].path field when it is a portable tracked repository path. Nested sourcePointers, staleArtifacts[].path, methods, prose, workspace/private paths, and any other field are never harvested as tracked authority; an unknown ID, cycle, missing tracked top-level path, or omitted blob blocks allocation
assignmentAuthoritySlicePolicy.trackedAuthorityBlobRule: trackedAuthorityBlobs is an ordinal path-sorted unique array of exact requiredTrackedAuthorityBlobKeys rows derived by literal tree lookup at authorityRevision. Every row is objectType blob, gitMode exactly 100644, gitBlobSha1 is the literal Git blob OID, and gitBlobSha256 is the lowercase SHA-256 of literal cat-file bytes; the held clean working file separately hashes to the same clean object. Missing, extra, executable, symlink, submodule, tree, LFS pointer, mode-only drift, raw-byte drift, case collision, or filter substitution blocks
assignmentAuthoritySlicePolicy.diagnosticPolicyRule: selectedVerificationPolicies contains exactly one key/object for every diagnosticPolicy referenced by the assigned row's ordered structured commands; unknown, missing, extra, or drifted policy blocks
assignmentAuthoritySlicePolicy.generatedPlanRule: generatedAssignmentSlice is null for ordinary rows and the exact parsed accepted-plan slice for a generated child; its raw digest and the accepted plan raw digest are separately assignment-bound
assignmentAuthoritySlicePolicy.hashRule: authoritySliceSha256 is assignmentPolicy.canonicalJsonDigestRule over exactly requiredAuthoritySliceKeys; the assignment packet and lane.local both contain that non-null digest and it participates in assignmentDigest
assignmentAuthoritySlicePolicy.revalidationRule: after every focused step and at check/handoff finalization, re-read current main and rederive the complete authority slice plus every tracked authority blob from current HEAD and the working tree under held allocation state; any target, policy, selected evidence row or source layer, tracked authority blob, work-item row, generated plan/slice, index flag, ref race, or working-byte mutation revokes, while an unrelated main commit with an identical slice remains legal

bootstrapFoundationPolicy.implementationTreeRule: implementationTree contains exactly candidatePaths in the same ordinal order. Each exact-key row is derived by literal tree lookup at implementationRevision: path equals the candidate path, gitMode is exactly 100644, storedBlobOid is Git's lowercase SHA-1 blob object ID, and storedBlobSha256 is the lowercase SHA-256 of literal cat-file bytes. Symlink, submodule, executable-mode, missing, extra, duplicate, case-colliding, LFS-pointer, or non-blob entries fail. implementationTreeSha256 is assignmentPolicy.canonicalJsonDigestRule over the exact implementationTree array, and changedPaths equals candidatePaths byte-for-byte
bootstrapFoundationPolicy.attemptRule: attemptId is exactly 32 lowercase hexadecimal characters freshly generated by the integration owner before PREPARED and never reused. Every attempt artifact is below workspace/logs/P0-AGENTS-001/bootstrap/attempts/<attempt-id>/ at one policy-fixed filename, where <attempt-id> expands exactly as privateWritePolicy.templatePlaceholderRule; retry uses a new attemptId and therefore never overwrites, substitutes, or ambiguously reuses preserved failure evidence. The sole non-attempt bootstrap artifact is the terminal completion copy fixed by terminalArtifactRule
bootstrapFoundationPolicy.receiptReferenceRule: repositoryBinding, integratedMainRepositoryBinding, canonicalMainRepositoryBinding, focusedVerificationReceipt, implementationReview.receipt, the nested implementation-review verificationReceipt, and journal are exact assignmentPolicy.digestReferencePolicy objects below workspace/logs/P0-AGENTS-001/bootstrap/attempts/<attempt-id>/ under privateWritePolicy.templatePlaceholderRule. repositoryBinding.path is bootstrap/attempts/<attempt-id>/repository-binding.json, its sha256 equals repositoryBindingSha256, and its bytes validate bootstrap-candidate-v1 at C. integratedMainRepositoryBinding.path is bootstrap/attempts/<attempt-id>/integrated-main-repository-binding.json, its sha256 equals integratedMainRepositoryBindingSha256, and its bytes validate canonical-main-v1 at C immediately after integration. canonicalMainRepositoryBinding.path is bootstrap/attempts/<attempt-id>/canonical-main-repository-binding.json, its sha256 equals canonicalMainRepositoryBindingSha256, and its bytes validate canonical-main-v1 at parkingRevision P. journal.path is bootstrap/attempts/<attempt-id>/journal.jsonl and its raw digest covers the terminal PARKED record. focusedVerificationReceipt.path is one immutable bootstrap/attempts/<attempt-id>/check/runs/<run-id>/verification-run-receipt.json in bootstrap-candidate-v1/check mode; implementationReview.receipt.path is bootstrap/attempts/<attempt-id>/implementation-review.json and validates implementationReviewSchema with result ACCEPT, while that payload's verificationReceipt.path is one immutable bootstrap/attempts/<attempt-id>/independent-review/runs/<run-id>/verification-run-receipt.json in bootstrap-candidate-v1/independent-review mode with PASS. All references are re-read and cross-bind the same attempt, authority, candidate, implementation/tree, integration, parking, and binding identities; implementationReview.reviewerId/result equal its typed payload, implementationReview.reviewedRevision and payload implementationRevision both equal outer implementationRevision, and the reviewer differs from the integration owner and later completion reviewer. The outer bootstrap receipt result is exactly PASS and is written atomically only after PARKED
bootstrapFoundationPolicy.authorizationRule: let A be the clean current refs/heads/main commit containing this exact policy while P0-AGENTS-001 is pending/unassigned with null assignee and empty ownedPaths. A is authorizationRevision and remains current main throughout candidate synthesis, provisional verification, and implementation review; any main advance, dirty index/worktree, authority-slice drift, prior durable bootstrap assignment, or non-matching row blocks and requires a fresh candidate from the new A
bootstrapFoundationPolicy.candidateSynthesisRule: the integration owner creates one new sibling worktree and one branch from A and synthesizes exactly one non-merge commit C whose sole parent is A and whose changed path set is exactly candidatePaths under ownershipPathIdentityRule. Prior experimental bytes may be read as an untrusted input, but no old worktree, branch, assignment packet, handoff, receipt, or commit identity grants authority. implementationRevision is C and the candidate is never executed before its complete bootstrap-candidate-v1 repository binding is privately sealed
bootstrapFoundationPolicy.integrationRule: only after the focused receipt is PASS and the distinct implementation review is ACCEPT for the exact C may the integration owner, while main is still clean at A, compare-and-swap fast-forward refs/heads/main and its checked-out tree from A to C with no merge, cherry-pick, rewritten commit, manual edit, or different tree. The owner immediately discards the provisional binding, derives a fresh canonical-main-v1 binding at C, and creates one direct-child parking commit P changing only orchestration/work-items.json: P0-AGENTS-001 becomes status verification, ownership state independent-verification, assignee null, ownedPaths empty, and has the sole blocker 'awaiting independently reviewed bootstrap completion receipt'. No other ledger byte may change. The owner then derives the final fresh canonical-main-v1 binding at P recorded by canonicalMainRepositoryBinding and seals the PARKED journal/bootstrap receipt. The later completion transition is a separately reviewed ledger-only direct child of P
bootstrapFoundationPolicy.terminalArtifactRule: after PARKED and after atomically sealing the attempt-scoped bootstrap-foundation.json, the owner harness creates workspace/logs/P0-AGENTS-001/bootstrap/bootstrap-foundation.json exactly once as a byte-identical atomic copy. It is absent before PARKED, is reserved only for this terminal publication, is never opened to a child, is never replaced or deleted, and completion.bootstrapReceipt.path must equal that concrete portable path with the copied raw SHA-256. Failed or retryable attempts never create it
bootstrapFoundationPolicy.failureRule: a failed synthesis, binding, focused check, review, or A-to-C compare-and-swap never advances main and never reuses or repairs C in place. Preserve the failed private journal/receipts for diagnosis, revoke the candidate, remove its registration only after exact path/identity checks, and resynthesize a new direct-child candidate from the still-current A or a newly authorized main commit; a candidate whose durable state is ambiguous is quarantined rather than resumed
bootstrapFoundationPolicy.journalRecordRule: each JSONL record has exactly requiredJournalRecordKeys; schema/version/attempt/work-item/authorization/lane/branch remain identical; sequence is a non-boolean integer equal to its 1-based journalStates position and state equals that position. recordedAtUtc is strict UTC YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.ffffffZ and strictly increases. laneDirectoryName is P0-AGENTS-001-<attempt-id> and branch is bootstrap/P0-AGENTS-001/<attempt-id>, with both placeholders expanded by privateWritePolicy.templatePlaceholderRule. The eight conditional transaction fields are non-null exactly when listed by journalStateNonNullFields for that state, retain identical earlier values, and otherwise are null; focusedVerificationRunId is 32 lowercase hex, revisions are lowercase 40-hex, and digests lowercase 64-hex. previousRecordSha256 is null only for PREPARED and otherwise equals raw SHA-256 of the immediately preceding complete JSONL line including LF. recordPayloadSha256 equals assignmentPolicy.canonicalJsonDigestRule over journalRecordPayloadKeys. Each full record is encoded as the same canonical compact ASCII JSON plus one LF, appended with write-through while the journal handle and parent are held; duplicate/missing/out-of-order/extra records or bytes fail
bootstrapFoundationPolicy.journalRule: the private append-only bootstrap journal validates journalRecordRule and permits only the complete listed state prefix. PREPARED proves no branch/worktree/admin entry exists; ASSIGNMENT_COMMITTED means A is durable but no create was attempted; CREATE_STARTED precedes the first worktree/branch mutation; BOUND proves candidate C and repository-binding.json; VERIFY_STARTED precedes execution; VERIFIED binds the PASS run by focusedVerificationRunId and the raw digest of its policy-fixed check/runs/<focusedVerificationRunId>/verification-run-receipt.json; REVIEWED binds ACCEPT review and its independently runId-addressed verification receipt; INTEGRATION_STARTED precedes the A-to-C CAS; INTEGRATED proves clean main C and the digest of integrated-main-repository-binding.json; PARKING_STARTED precedes C-to-P; PARKED proves clean main P and canonical-main-repository-binding.json. Every policy-fixed attempt path, including each runId-qualified path, is re-read for every recorded digest. Before CREATE_STARTED, resume is permitted only after re-proving absence. CREATE_STARTED through REVIEWED ambiguity follows failureRule without advancing main. At INTEGRATION_STARTED, exact main A permits retry of the same CAS, exact main C permits appending INTEGRATED after full revalidation, and anything else blocks owner intervention. At INTEGRATED/PARKING_STARTED, exact main C permits only the deterministic parking retry, exact main P permits appending PARKED, and anything else blocks. Main is never rolled back from a proven C/P transition
bootstrapFoundationPolicy.rule: this is the sole self-hosting exception and authorizes only the exact authorization, synthesis, binding, verification, review, integration, parking, failure, and journal transitions above. It cannot allocate, complete, or authorize any other row

verificationCommandPolicy.runtimeTreeDigestRule: Python base/environment/selected-module trees admit at most 10000 files, 1 GiB total file bytes, and 512 MiB per file and reject reparses, non-directories, multi-link files, case-fold collisions, every __pycache__/.pytest_cache component, and every pyc/pyo file rather than excluding it. Include every admitted directory as UTF-8 D<NUL><forward-slash-relative-path><LF> and every admitted file as F<NUL><path><NUL><decimal-size><NUL><raw-lowercase-SHA256><LF>, ordinal-sort all rows by relative path, concatenate, and take lowercase SHA-256. Every admitted Python tree is complete and follows a deliberate clean bootstrap. Open/hold every nested directory/file without share-delete through child drain, then re-enumerate/reopen the identical path/identity/content set. Non-OS native trees instead use nativeTreeHardlinkPolicy; Windows-serviced OS executables/trees use osNativeIdentityPolicy
verificationCommandPolicy.controlPlaneLauncherRule: normal lifecycle allocate/resume/preflight/check/handoff starts only from the clean canonical-main tools/work-item-lane.ps1 and tools/work-item-lane.py bytes; a worker-lane command supplies exactly one explicit absolute target lane path to that main launcher and never executes either worker copy. Under native System32 Windows PowerShell with NoLogo, NoProfile, NonInteractive, and Bypass for that file only, the launcher validates the canonical host/signature and the complete owner-held repositoryBinding before any repository-trusting Git read, holds/revalidates the tracked launcher/tool and stable Git topology, then hashes the exact pinned base CPython executable and complete runtime tree before directly invoking the held main lifecycle tool with -I -S -B. Bootstrap-candidate-v1 is the sole exception: an owner-side driver binds the already-synthesized direct-child candidate commit and invokes its held candidate launcher/tool only for provisional bootstrap verification. The py launcher, worker control-plane copy in normal mode, python from PATH, PowerShell profile, alternate host, or caller-supplied interpreter/bootstrap is forbidden
verificationCommandPolicy.controlPlaneHostAliasRule: the powershell executable binding is an os-native-executable role governed by osNativeIdentityPolicy; the invoked alias is exactly the native System32 WindowsPowerShell/v1.0/powershell.exe path. The tracked launcher and pinned Python/runtime files remain plain non-reparse single-link files
verificationCommandPolicy.controlPlaneTrustBoundary: the native Microsoft-signed System32 Windows PowerShell, Win32 filesystem identity APIs, the owner-side repository binding, and the clean canonical-main control-plane blobs are the explicit trust anchors until the pinned CPython/Git bindings take over; the worker Git pointer and worker control-plane copies are never roots of trust. This is a cooperative repository admission boundary, not resistance to a compromised operating system or malicious integration owner
verificationCommandPolicy.targetRule: a module target is one exact role-allowlisted token; an unowned script target's clean-filtered blob identity from bound Git hash-object --path must equal the assignment-commit blob while its raw checkout identity is separately held, and an owned script target is the exact bound pre-sequence raw file; every script is one canonical portable repository-relative literal path with the declared extension and a plain single-link identity
verificationCommandPolicy.argumentRule: args is an array of at most 128 ASCII strings of at most 4096 characters each with no NUL, CR, or LF; drive-qualified, UNC, rooted, tilde, URI, percent-expansion, dollar-expansion, and PowerShell environment forms are forbidden; path-like values are canonical portable repository/workspace-relative literals; every value is passed verbatim and the exact Windows CreateProcess rendered executable-plus-argv, including fixed bootstrap flags/targets and terminal NUL, must not exceed 30000 UTF-16 code units
verificationCommandPolicy.stepDigestRule: stepSha256 is assignmentPolicy.canonicalJsonDigestRule over the exact requiredStepKeys projection of one parsed step
verificationCommandPolicy.commandDigestRule: verificationCommandSha256 is assignmentPolicy.canonicalJsonDigestRule over one exact requiredCommandKeys command object; verificationCommandsSha256 is the same digest over the complete ordered verificationCommands array; a source receipt selects exactly verifierCommandIndex before hashing that one command
verificationCommandPolicy.pytestCacheRule: every structured step with invocation module and target pytest, or invocation script/target tools/run-focused-tests.py with first arg pytest, contains the exact adjacent args pair '-p', 'no:cacheprovider' exactly once, also runs with PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 and PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1 from the fixed bootstrap, and rejects any .pytest_cache/__pycache__/pyc/pyo event in the complete private/worktree write audits. A pytest command without all three independent controls is invalid before execution
verificationCommandPolicy.focusedTestRunnerRule: tools/run-focused-tests.py is a tracked 100644 non-LFS script admitted only under python/retail-python hermetic profiles. Its args are exactly <framework> <one-or-more selectors/flags> --marker <marker>, with --marker occurring once as the final pair; framework is unittest or pytest; marker is one 1..256-character printable ASCII line matching ^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*(?: [A-Z][A-Z0-9_=:.\/-]*)* PASS$ and expectedMarkers is exactly [marker]. The runner accepts no code string, eval, response file, path escape, environment-selected plugin, or additional framework. It uses unittest's name loader or the already-bound pytest module, returns the framework's nonzero code unchanged, and only after zero success writes exactly marker plus LF to stdout as the final non-empty stdout line. Pytest invocations also satisfy pytestCacheRule. This converts framework-variable summaries/stderr into one deterministic harness marker without treating stderr or a test-count prefix as acceptance

verificationRunReceiptPolicy.verificationModeDispatchRule: modeValues equals the exact key set of verificationModeDispatch. A run's repositoryBinding.mode, worktreeWriteAudit.mode, phase, and assignmentDigest follow exactly its one row; phases preserve the listed semantic order and no pair outside a row is legal. lane-completion-required-otherwise-null means non-null equal to the original assignment only when completionReceipt.mode is lane-v1 and null for every other completion mode. Handoff pre/post references require worker-lane-v1/precommit or postcommit; bootstrap focused requires bootstrap-candidate-v1/check and bootstrap implementation-review verification requires bootstrap-candidate-v1/independent-review; feature proposal/materialization require canonical-main-readonly-v1/propose and canonical-main-materialization-v1/materialize or resume; completion verification requires canonical-main-completion-v1/completion. Source/dimension evidence names the already typed run appropriate to the producing transaction; it cannot override dispatch
verificationRunReceiptPolicy.runIdRule: runId is exactly 32 lowercase hexadecimal characters freshly generated by the harness before reserving outputs, unique for the work item, and never reused. Every success or failure artifact for that invocation is immutable below its runId directory; retry always uses a new runId and cannot overwrite, delete, reinterpret, or substitute an earlier run
verificationRunReceiptPolicy.outputRule: capture stdout/stderr as raw bytes from process creation through complete Job drain without early marker success. Configure the bound child/wrapper for UTF-8, reject BOM, NUL, invalid UTF-8, and bare CR, and split only LF/CRLF after strict decoding. Enforce maxStdoutBytesPerStep, maxStderrBytesPerStep, and maxDecodedLinesPerStep independently; on first overflow terminate/drain the Job, retain the exact bounded prefix, set outputTruncated true, and FAIL with OUTPUT_LIMIT. PASS requires outputTruncated false. expectedMarkers match complete decoded stdout lines exactly in declared order, the last expected marker is the final non-empty stdout line, stderr never satisfies a marker, and terminal status is recognized only when a complete trimmed line is exactly PASS/FAIL/SKIP or matches ^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_.:-]*(?: [A-Z][A-Z0-9_.:-]*)* (PASS|FAIL|SKIP)$. Thus lowercase words, failed=0, counts, substrings, and prose do not become terminal statuses; any recognized FAIL/SKIP line anywhere contradicts PASS
verificationRunReceiptPolicy.rule: the receipt and every nested row have exactly their required keys and mode/phase are listed values permitted by verificationModeDispatch. repositoryBinding, trackedWorktreeBinding, privateWriteAudit, worktreeWriteAudit, stdout, and stderr are assignmentPolicy.digestReferencePolicy objects; trackedWorktreeBinding.sha256 equals trackedWorktreeBindingSha256 and validates trackedWorktreeBindingPolicy for this run. A step toolchainAttestation is non-null only when a complete authentic attestation for the selected profile's harness/wrapper mode was produced and serialized; it is null when none exists. Null plus failed process creation requires exitCode null, result FAIL, and PRELAUNCH_FAILURE; null after process creation requires result FAIL and TOOLCHAIN_FAILURE plus every other applicable reason. PASS always requires a non-null valid attestation. toolchainAttestations is the identical execution-order projection of only non-null step references. commandRuns has exactly one 1-based row per ordered command and stepRuns exactly one 1-based row per attempted ordered step, with canonical command/step digests, declared timeout/markers/diagnostics, integer exit code except prelaunch, strict booleans, and reasons as a unique failureReasonValues-order array. PASS has empty reasons and requires every declared step ran PASS, exit code zero, no timeout/truncation, outputRule and diagnostic policy passed, both write audits passed, identities stayed fixed, and no required stage was skipped; FAIL has the exact complete applicable reason-code set. assignmentDigest follows verificationModeDispatch. All other hashes are lowercase fixed-width and gitRevision is the exact checked revision. Failure receipts remain immutable diagnostic evidence and cannot satisfy acceptance
verificationRunReceiptPolicy.pathRule: ordinary/owner runs place the preserved receipt and every artifact below workspace/logs/<work-item-id>/<phase>/runs/<run-id>/; repositoryBinding, tracked-worktree-binding.json, privateWriteAudit, worktreeWriteAudit, command streams, and toolchain files use their policy-fixed names there. Bootstrap-candidate-v1 retains its attempt-level repository-binding.json and places tracked-worktree-binding.json, the preserved receipt, and all audits/streams/toolchain files below bootstrap/attempts/<attempt-id>/<phase>/runs/<run-id>/ for the exact dispatch phases check and independent-review; ordinary <phase>/runs/<run-id>/ templates are not expanded for bootstrap-candidate-v1. Every placeholder follows privateWritePolicy.templatePlaceholderRule, every exact path is expanded and reserved before child launch, and a phase directory or runs parent is never itself a write grant

trackedWorktreeBindingPolicy.rule: derive entries as the ordinal path-sorted exact union of every tracked path in literal HEAD and index for the bound worktree, with Git rename detection disabled and no case-fold collision. Head/index modes/OIDs come from literal trees; each is either null when absent or a regular 100644/100755 blob, never symlink/submodule/tree. PRESENT has non-null working clean/raw/size/volume/file/link fields, rejects every reparse component, and requires workingLinkCount exactly 1; DELETED has all working fields null and is legal only for an ordinal-exact assigned deletion already authorized by ownershipPathIdentityRule. Unowned paths are PRESENT and clean-equal HEAD/index. Dirty owned paths retain their exact index/working identities. ownerMutablePaths is empty for every run except canonical-main-materialization-v1, where it is exactly the three allowed tracked paths. Before child creation, hold the worktree root, every directory, and every PRESENT file with no share-write/delete and revalidate all entries through Job drain, preventing indirect checker/test/import/data substitution. The child process always has zero tracked-write authority. For materialization, the child emits only private proposal bytes; after Job drain the owner revalidates, releases only the three mutable file handles, performs the exact isolated-index CAS itself while parent directories and all other files remain held, then reopens/rebinds all three. Any temporary mutation, outside alias, restored substitution, missing handle, or inventory drift fails
trackedWorktreeBindingPolicy.digestRule: trackedWorktreeBindingSha256 is assignmentPolicy.canonicalJsonDigestRule over the exact complete binding object; trackedWorktreeBinding is its path/raw-SHA reference and every run/audit cross-binds both

handoffReceiptPolicy.rule: the receipt has exactly requiredReceiptKeys and PASS is the only acceptance result. baseRevision is the assignment commit; implementationRevision is its sole non-merge direct child; implementationTreeOid is the literal Git tree OID; changedPaths is the non-empty ordinal exact owned-path delta under ownershipPathIdentityRule. The precommit and postcommit references validate verificationRunReceiptPolicy at baseRevision and implementationRevision respectively with identical assignment/authority/repository/protected identities. requiredOutputDimensions is the assigned exact six-key map, dimensionReceipts follows evidenceDimensionPolicy handoff shape, artifactDigests follows completionReceiptPolicy.artifactDigestRule, both write-audit references validate their named PASS schemas, and every identity is re-read at handoff

verificationCommandPolicy.executionRule: execute at most 16 steps by direct bound executable-plus-argv invocation with no shell, eval, encoded command, response file, py launcher, or ledger-supplied command string; hold executable/runtime/archive bindings for the sequence, use one sequence-wide timeout, stop at first nonzero step, and contain/drain the Windows Job process tree
verificationCommandPolicy.markerRule: verificationRunReceiptPolicy.outputRule is the sole marker/terminal grammar: expected markers are complete stdout lines in declared order with the final expected marker last, stderr cannot satisfy them, and any recognized terminal FAIL/SKIP or forbidden diagnostic fails even after an earlier PASS line
verificationCommandPolicy.trustBoundary: cooperative-code and process-tree boundary, not an operating-system or filesystem sandbox; wrapper attestations declare descendant tool identity but cannot prove absence of hostile filesystem syscalls, so revalidate the exact repository binding, live main authority slice, main cleanliness, owned targets, finite protected state, and tool identities after every step
verificationCommandPolicy.runtimeNullabilityRule: every requiredRuntimeBindingKeys field is present. os-native-executable is legal only for cmd/powershell and has all eight path/digest fields null; os-native-tree and native-tree have non-null executableRoot/executableTreeSha256 and all environment/archive/canary fields null; python-isolated-archive has non-null executableRoot/executableTreeSha256/moduleArchivePath/moduleArchiveSha256 and null environment/canary fields; python-isolated-environment has non-null executableRoot/executableTreeSha256/environmentRoot/environmentTreeSha256/canaryReceiptPath/canaryReceiptSha256 and null module-archive fields. hardlinkAliasSetSha256 is non-null exactly for os-native-executable, os-native-tree, and native-tree executable rows and equals the executable's complete policy-specific alias-set digest; it is null for Python executable kinds, which remain single-link. Role/kind must equal roleRuntimeKinds and no implicit sibling runtime is allowed

nativeTreeHardlinkPolicy.fileIdentityRule: volume serial is exactly 16 lowercase hexadecimal digits and the 128-bit Win32 file ID exactly 32 lowercase hexadecimal digits; file identity text is <volume-serial>:<file-id>. linkCount is a non-boolean positive integer
nativeTreeHardlinkPolicy.aliasSetDigestRule: for each distinct file identity, enumerate every hardlink name on the volume with native Win32 APIs, require the count equals linkCount and is at most maxAliasesPerFileIdentity, resolve every alias without reparses to a regular file below the one held bound native-tree root, require every alias to appear exactly once in the complete tree inventory with the identical identity/size/raw SHA-256, emit UTF-8 A<NUL><forward-slash-root-relative-path><LF> rows in ordinal order, concatenate, and take lowercase SHA-256. Any inaccessible, omitted, extra, outside-root, case-colliding, cross-volume, reparse, or identity/content-mismatched alias fails
nativeTreeHardlinkPolicy.treeDigestRule: under nativeTreeBounds emit D<NUL><relative-path><LF> for every directory and F<NUL><relative-path><NUL><decimal-size><NUL><raw-lowercase-SHA256><NUL><file-identity><NUL><decimal-link-count><NUL><hardlink-alias-set-sha256><LF> for every file path, ordinal-sort all rows by relative path, concatenate as UTF-8, and take lowercase SHA-256. A single-link file still has a one-row alias set. Hold the root, every nested directory, and every alias path without share-delete through complete Job drain, then re-enumerate/reopen and require identical directories, alias sets, identities, sizes, bytes, and digest. This permits legitimate in-distribution hardlinks such as Git-for-Windows aliases without trusting a link outside the admitted root

osNativeIdentityPolicy.aliasSetDigestRule: enumerate every hardlink name for the bound volume/file identity with the native Win32 API; normalize each absolute path only after exact no-reparse resolution below one approvedAliasRoots value, require every row to repeat the identical volume/file/link-count/size/raw-byte identity, ordinal-sort exact requiredAliasRowKeys rows by path, and take assignmentPolicy.canonicalJsonDigestRule. The enumerated row count equals linkCount and is at most maxAliasesPerFile; an inaccessible, omitted, extra, cross-volume, outside-root, reparse, unsigned, or identity-mismatched alias fails
osNativeIdentityPolicy.executableRule: cmd resolves exactly to native System32/cmd.exe and powershell exactly to native System32/WindowsPowerShell/v1.0/powershell.exe; each is Authenticode-valid under the current Windows trusted publisher chain, its signer/leaf certificate/thumbprint/timestamp status is captured in the private binding evidence, and hardlinkAliasSetSha256 binds its complete approved servicing alias set. This is explicit signed-operating-system trust, not a claim that the file is single-link
osNativeIdentityPolicy.treeDigestRule: an os-native-tree root uses nativeTreeBounds and rejects reparses, case-fold collisions, non-directories, and aliases outside approvedAliasRoots. Emit D<NUL><relative-path><LF> for every directory and F<NUL><relative-path><NUL><decimal-size><NUL><raw-lowercase-SHA256><NUL><volume-serial><NUL><file-id><NUL><decimal-link-count><NUL><hardlink-alias-set-sha256><LF> for every file; ordinal-sort rows by relative path, concatenate as UTF-8, and take lowercase SHA-256. Every file is Authenticode-valid when signable or inherits the validated signed Windows component/package identity recorded by the owner; every alias set is complete. Hold every root/file and re-enumerate the complete tree and alias sets after Job drain

verificationCommandPolicy.nativeTreeRule: a native-tree or os-native-tree binding role must occur in nativeTreeRootKinds and resolves exactly by that locator: Git/Git-LFS use the HKLM Git-for-Windows InstallPath; Godot/Blender/FFmpeg use the owner-bound distribution root containing the executable and its distribution manifest; dotnet uses the host-resolved DOTNET_ROOT containing host/fxr/shared; MSBuild/C++ use one exact versioned VS installation/toolset returned by the bound vswhere identity; csharp-compiler uses its exact versioned Windows .NET Framework directory; Windows SDK uses the exact registered version root. Non-OS native-tree roles use nativeTreeHardlinkPolicy and are complete for their distribution/toolset root. csharp-compiler alone uses osNativeIdentityPolicy.treeDigestRule for its serviced Microsoft.NET version root; CLR/GAC/System32 components outside that root are explicitly part of the same signed-operating-system trust boundary and are not falsely claimed as descendants. Git additionally binds exact --exec-path inside its complete tree, git-lfs and every invoked helper. A wrapper executable SHA, guessed parent, omitted in-root descendant, outside-root hardlink, unmodeled out-of-root application dependency, or cap overflow never establishes identity

repositoryBindingPolicy.bindingTypeRule: volumeSerialNumber is exactly 16 lowercase hexadecimal characters, fileId exactly 32 lowercase hexadecimal characters, every Git revision/object ID exactly 40 lowercase hexadecimal characters, and every SHA-256 exactly 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters. reparseTag is the non-boolean integer zero; size is a non-boolean integer from 0 through 9223372036854775807; every stable/control working linkCount is the non-boolean integer 1; both control gitMode values are exactly the string 100644. Null, boolean-as-integer, uppercase, sign, prefix, coercion, and unbounded values fail; the separately OS-trusted PowerShell host-alias rule does not weaken these repository-row types
repositoryBindingPolicy.collectionRule: directories, stableAdministrativeFiles, mutableAdministrativePaths, absentAdministrativeNodes, and trackedControlPlaneFiles are each present and sorted by the ordinal tuple (role,path), using absolutePath for tracked-control path; no array has a duplicate or case-fold path collision. Each fixed role occurs exactly once; common-info-file and common-objects-info-file may repeat only with unique role/path pairs and must equal their complete admitted inventories. Directory and mutable role sets equal the selected mode's exact role-set maps, every mutable row equals mutableAdministrativeRolePolicy for its role, and tracked control roles equal trackedControlPlaneRoles
repositoryBindingPolicy.modeRule: mode is one modes value and all conditional fields are explicit rather than omitted. canonical-main-v1 has laneRevision and laneHead null and no lane-role row; workItemId is null only for the non-mutating list operation and otherwise is one exact selected work-item ID. worker-lane-v1 and bootstrap-candidate-v1 require non-null workItemId/laneRevision/laneHead and their exact lane role sets. mainHead/laneHead transitionRule values equal the selected mode/operation set in headTransitionRuleSets; authorityRevision/mainRevision/start commits satisfy headTransitionRule, and bootstrap revisions satisfy bootstrapRule
repositoryBindingPolicy.pathRule: every field named path or absolutePath is canonical absolute Windows text in this private binding; repositoryRelativePath is canonical portable forward-slash text and equals its role's tracked policy path. Every component is opened without following reparses, reparseTag is zero, role/path pairs and path identities are ordinal unique, and required mode-specific rows are exact set-equal rather than a permissive subset
repositoryBindingPolicy.topologyRule: worker-lane-v1 and bootstrap-candidate-v1 bind the lane .git file, its resolved per-worktree Git directory, the gitdir and commondir pointer files, the common Git directory, and the main/lane worktree directory identities; raw pointer bytes must resolve exactly to the bound identities, the common directory is exactly the bound main .git directory, and the bound Git worktree registry contains exactly the expected root, branch, and start commit. canonical-main-v1 has no laneRevision/laneHead or lane-role rows; other modes require them
repositoryBindingPolicy.absenceRoleFormat: absent:<scope>:<forward-slash-relative-path>, where scope is common, main, or lane and separators/case are literal
repositoryBindingPolicy.absenceDerivationRule: absentAdministrativeNodes is exactly the ordinal (role,path) set derived from: every alwaysAbsentCommonNodes path under the common Git directory; every missing allowed common-info/common-objects-info member; lane config.worktree in linked modes; config.lock, packed-refs.lock, and shallow.lock under common; HEAD.lock and index.lock plus every operationAbsenceNames member under each active main/lane Git directory; and <bound-main-branch-ref>.lock, <bound-lane-branch-ref>.lock when linked, and <bound-upstream-main-ref>.lock. Additionally no administrative tree may contain any unlisted entry ending .lock or beginning BISECT_; such a node is an unknown-key-equivalent failure rather than an extension. Each derived row uses absenceRoleFormat and exact canonical path; no prose-selected absence is legal
repositoryBindingPolicy.administrativeClosureRule: stableAdministrativeFiles contains every fixed mandatory role. The present common info root is an exact flat subset of commonInfoAdmittedNames and the present common objects/info root is an exact flat subset of commonObjectsInfoAdmittedNames; each present member has one stable row and each missing allowed member has one derived absent row, while any directory, subpath, or unknown/case-colliding name fails. The bound git-hooks-sink directory has an exactly empty entry set. Presence of an omitted, extra, unbounded, included, graft, alternate, replacement, shallow, sparse, operation-in-progress, lock, or hook-sink child node revokes
repositoryBindingPolicy.configurationRule: common config is exact-key parsed from the held bytes. It may contain only the repository-format core keys with their current bound scalar values, remote <name> url/fetch, branch <name> remote/merge/vscode-merge-base, user name/email, lfs.repositoryformatversion, lfs.<url>.access, and exactly standardGitLfsConfig; extensions.worktreeConfig, include/includeIf, alias, core.worktree/hooksPath/fsmonitor/sshCommand/editor, gpg/program, credential helper, non-LFS filter/process/clean/smudge, and every other executable or unknown key are rejected. Standard LFS config may exist without execution; git-lfs becomes required and executable only when the bound committed attribute source selects filter=lfs for an exact operated path. Control-plane files reject every filter, LFS, ident, working-tree-encoding, or non-text/EOL attribute
repositoryBindingPolicy.gitEnvironmentRule: before every Git launch clear every inherited environment key whose ordinal-casefolded name starts with git_. Install exactly gitEnvironmentFixedValues plus all gitEnvironmentDynamicKeys resolved to the already held identities; no other Git key is present except GIT_ATTR_SOURCE during the single control-working-clean-object operation, where it equals that control row's revision. Every invocation uses the exact bound git.exe, explicit --git-dir/--work-tree identities, exact ordinal -c key=value arguments from gitCommandConfigFixedValues plus core.hooksPath=<bound-empty-sink>, and no shell or alias expansion
repositoryBindingPolicy.indexFlagRule: for both main and lane indexes, reject split-index, sparse-index, untracked-cache, fsmonitor extension/valid bits, assume-unchanged, skip-worktree, intent-to-add, stage other than zero outside an explicitly failed merge (which is already forbidden), duplicate/case-colliding entries, and any path outside the exact committed index universe. Bound Git ls-files --stage --debug -z plus write-tree are parsed independently before and after every step; no status-display convention is trusted
repositoryBindingPolicy.upstreamAncestryRule: upstream-main-ref is the exact loose refs/remotes/origin/main file named by held passive config and the assignment packet's upstreamMainCommit. It is stable within one lifecycle call, may move only by fast-forward between calls after an owner fetch under canonical-main binding, and current clean main plus lane assignment base must descend from the recorded commit; missing, packed-only, rewritten, alternate-remote, or unrecorded fetch state revokes
repositoryBindingPolicy.worktreeClosureRule: before and after every step, compare-and-swap, and Job drain, parse exact NUL-delimited HEAD-to-index and index-to-worktree raw diffs plus untracked/ignored inventories. Main is fully clean. A lane may differ only at exact ownedPaths during implementation and must be fully clean at handoff; every unowned tracked path retains its assignment blob/mode, and every created ignored/untracked path is authorized by the private/worktree write policies. A whole-lane Windows change watcher rejects any create/write/delete/rename event outside those scopes even when bytes are later restored
repositoryBindingPolicy.trackedControlPlaneRule: trackedControlPlaneFiles has exactly the two role rows. Normal modes bind the canonical-main launcher and lifecycle tool at authorityRevision and require current clean main to carry the identical literal stored blobs; bootstrap binds candidate copies at laneRevision. storedBlobOid/gitMode come from literal tree lookup, storedBlobSha256 from literal cat-file bytes, working fields from no-share held handles, and workingCleanObjectOid is separately computed only after administrative/config closure and equals storedBlobOid. Neither control file may be LFS, symlink, submodule, executable-mode drift, reparse, or multi-link
repositoryBindingPolicy.headTransitionRule: mainHead is refs/heads/main at mainRevision and may advance only to a clean descendant whose complete authority slice and bound control-plane blobs are identical; worker laneHead starts at laneRevision and remains there until the one allowed direct-child handoff transition, while bootstrap laneHead remains exactly its synthesized candidate. Mutable index/ref/packed-ref state is never trusted as immutable bytes: every transition uses explicit compare-and-swap and exact before/after HEAD, branch, index-tree, clean-state, lock-absence, ancestry, and changed-path checkpoints
repositoryBindingPolicy.holdAndRevalidateRule: open all stable files with neither FILE_SHARE_WRITE nor FILE_SHARE_DELETE and all bound directories with no share-delete handles before repository-trusting Git; hold the launcher, lifecycle tool, Git runtime, Python runtime tree, repository directories, pointers, configs, and stable inventories through complete descendant Job drain. Around every step, ref/index compare-and-swap, receipt write, and at finalization, hash held bytes, reopen every exact path, and require the same path, volume serial, file ID, link count, size, raw bytes, exact directory/inventory set, semantic mutable checkpoint, and absence set; any failure revokes before evidence can pass
repositoryBindingPolicy.assignmentRule: lane.local contains the exact repositoryBinding object; assignment.json contains its non-null canonical repositoryBindingSha256 and assignmentDigest covers that digest. The owner copy is authoritative and the lane copy must be byte-identical; once any repository binding, owner packet, or registered worktree entry becomes durable, a missing/replaced lane revokes and can be recovered only by a new assignment. A journaled allocation may materialize the lane exactly once only when its compare-and-swap journal proves that no prior binding, owner packet, or worktree-registry entry ever became durable. The toolchain binding manifest and every check/handoff receipt cross-bind repositoryBindingSha256
repositoryBindingPolicy.checkerEntryRule: an acceptance-capable ledger/onboarding checker runs only under a launcher-delivered repository and tool binding. A standalone diagnostic may resolve Git independently from the HKLM Git-for-Windows registration plus Win32 identity, compare it to the expected native-tree binding, and report diagnostics, but PATH-selected or unbound Git can never produce an acceptance PASS
repositoryBindingPolicy.bootstrapRule: bootstrap-candidate-v1 is owner-side only: authorityRevision and mainRevision are the clean committed authorization revision, laneRevision is its already-synthesized one-commit direct-child candidate, and the tracked control rows bind laneRevision without embedding their own digest in tracked bytes. The private binding and provisional focused receipt remain under the main work-item log, bootstrapFoundation.repositoryBindingSha256 binds them, and an independent typed review is required before integration; after integration this candidate binding is discarded and canonical-main-v1 is freshly derived

verificationCommandPolicy.pythonBootstrapBindingRule: pythonBootstrapSha256 is always the non-null lowercase SHA-256 of the UTF-8 fixed bootstrap embedded in the assigned tools/work-item-lane.py blob; it appears in lane.local and the assignment packet, participates in assignmentDigest, and is rederived before every step and handoff
verificationCommandPolicy.pythonModuleArchiveRule: the archive is a raw-SHA-addressed ZIP under the immutable main workspace/logs/<work-item-id>/toolchain tree and is generated from the complete bound pytest, _pytest, pluggy, packaging, iniconfig, pygments, and colorama pure-Python roots plus the exact matching dist-info metadata. The pinned pytest 9.1.1 METADATA dependency closure is parsed and must equal those admitted distributions after marker evaluation on the bound Windows CPython; a missing, extra, transitive, native, or ambient dependency fails. Its canonical manifest binds every distribution/version, source path/raw SHA-256, archive path/raw SHA-256, and metadata dependency edge. Entries are ordinal forward-slash unique regular files, STORE-only, fixed 2000-01-01 UTC timestamps, create_system=0, zero internal/external attributes and comments/extras, and exact admitted flags; only .py and explicitly modeled pure data/dist-info files are legal. A directory entry, symlink bit, native pyd/dll, cache/bytecode path, unknown extension, duplicate/case collision, unmanifested metadata field, or different module origin fails
verificationCommandPolicy.retailPythonRuntimeRule: retail-python directly binds the pinned main venv Scripts/python.exe, its resolved complete base CPython tree, and the complete admitted venv tree including Scripts, site-packages, native pyd/dll files, and distribution metadata; any bytecode/cache node or reparse fails instead of being omitted. -I -S -B uses the fixed bootstrap to add only that fully bound site-packages tree after the bound standard-library roots and before repository roots, with no module archive
verificationCommandPolicy.retailPythonCanaryRule: allocation writes one canonical private canary receipt at workspace/logs/<work-item-id>/toolchain/retail-python-canary.json after the fixed isolated bootstrap imports exactly PIL, PIL._imaging, fontTools, defusedxml, and pytest; every module row binds exact version, canonical environment-relative origin, origin raw SHA-256, and native status, while the receipt binds executable/base-tree/environment-tree identities and PASS; runtime canaryReceiptPath/raw SHA-256 are non-null for retail-python and null for other kinds, participate in assignmentDigest, and every pre/post execution canary must reproduce the exact receipt bytes
verificationCommandPolicy.toolchainDeliveryRule: after hashing the exact ledger step the harness writes the canonical binding manifest at workspace/logs/<work-item-id>/<phase>/runs/<run-id>/toolchain/command-<two-digit-command>-step-<two-digit-step>-bindings.json and reserves/holds the sibling attestation file; bootstrap uses the exact bootstrap/attempts/<attempt-id>/<phase>/runs/<run-id>/toolchain/ form. All placeholders follow privateWritePolicy.templatePlaceholderRule. For every child, PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_HANDLE_LIST contains exactly a NUL-read stdin handle plus the stdout/stderr pipe write handles; parent read ends are non-inheritable. For wrapper mode it additionally contains exactly the dedicated attestation-pipe write handle, supplied as OPENBFME_TOOLCHAIN_ATTESTATION_PIPE; harness mode supplies that environment key as an empty string and has no attestation pipe. The harness clears all inherited OPENBFME_TOOLCHAIN_* variables and injects exactly toolchainDeliveryEnvironmentKeys including commandIndex/stepIndex; canonical absolute paths exist only in private environment values, never argv. In wrapper mode the bound wrapper writes exactly an 8-lowercase-hex byte length plus LF, at most 1 MiB of canonical JSON payload, then EOF and never writes a receipt file; the harness drains all pipes/Job, validates it, then writes those exact bytes through its reserved handle. In harness mode the harness itself derives the exact attestation payload from the already-held binding manifest and observed direct/auxiliary process identities after Job drain and writes it through that handle; it never claims wrapper observation. Both modes flush, close, and re-read the receipt. Delivery metadata is outside stepSha256 but bound through run/tool/authority/repository/protected identities and bindingManifestSha256. Unknown or missing standard/attestation handles, undeclared inheritance, run/phase/index/profile/step drift, pre-existing bytes, or payload mismatch fails closed
verificationCommandPolicy.pythonBootstrapRule: the harness invokes the owner-bound python.exe directly with -I -S -B and one fixed tracked bootstrap whose digest is assignment-bound. Because -B suppresses writes but does not prevent bytecode loading, allocation rejects every cache/pyc/pyo node in each admitted base/environment/module-source tree. sys.path is rebuilt in this exact precedence: the isolated original standard-library/native roots from the bound base runtime, then either the locked pure-module archive or completely bound retail site-packages, then the bound repository importer root, then repository root; every other original or ambient entry is rejected. Canary/hostile checks prove pathlib, subprocess, socket, and other standard-library modules resolve inside the bound base tree and cannot be shadowed by dependency or repository roots; ambient site, user site, PYTHONPATH, startup hooks, and ledger-supplied code strings are forbidden
verificationCommandPolicy.scriptTargetRule: each script target has exactly requiredScriptTargetBindingKeys. Literal assignment tree lookup must be type blob and gitMode is the exact role-admitted string 100644 unless that role explicitly requires 100755; assignmentBlobOid is the literal Git blob OID and assignmentBlobSha256 is the lowercase SHA-256 of the exact literal cat-file blob bytes. 120000 symlink, 160000 submodule, tree, missing, and mode transition are rejected even when Windows checks out a symlink blob as a plain file. workingCleanObjectOid is separately computed with the bound committed attribute source and equals assignmentBlobOid, while raw checkout bytes, file identity, size, and single link are separately held/revalidated. Non-LFS targets have null LFS fields and reject filter/LFS attributes; LFS targets bind the literal pointer mode/OID/SHA separately from hydrated bytes/local-object identity and require bound git-lfs. Every target binding and run receipt carries gitMode
verificationCommandPolicy.gitLfsBindingRule: git-lfs is a distinct exact executable binding and attested role; it is conditionally required whenever Git attributes select the LFS filter for a script target, owned path, protected path, commit write, or verification input, and the canonical pointer plus local object identity must validate before and after use; absent, ambient, substituted, or unreported git-lfs fails closed
verificationCommandPolicy.csharpCompilerBindingRule: when Windows PowerShell Add-Type is used, csharp-compiler is the exact csc.exe descendant resolved during allocation from the bound PowerShell/.NET framework environment, bound and held by canonical path, raw SHA-256, file identity, link count, versioned parent runtime-tree digest, and wrapper attestation; onboarding-contract-v1 requires it, and an in-process compile, alternate compiler, ambient PATH substitution, or unreported compiler descendant fails closed

protectedStatePolicy.rule: protected state is an ordinal unique finite read-only file list derived only from accepted-plan sealedInputArtifacts and, for rotwk-gate-v1, the exact selection plus its directly referenced manifests; there is no free-form declared-private-input class. A pre-plan command that needs any other private input is unallocatable until the integration owner adds a typed canonical derivation rather than letting the worker declare it. Work-item artifacts are outputs and never protected inputs, while harness receipts/toolchain files are writes. Recursive content-pack, workspace, environment, repository, or arbitrary directory hashing is forbidden, tool runtimes are bound separately, and protectedStateSha256 canonically hashes the exact entry array

privateWritePolicy.templatePlaceholderRule: the only template placeholders are <work-item-id>, <phase>, <run-id>, <attempt-id>, <two-digit-command>, and <two-digit-step>. They expand respectively to the exact selected work-item ID; exact verificationModeDispatch phase; validated runId; validated bootstrap attemptId; and the 1-based commandIndex/stepIndex formatted as exactly two ASCII decimal digits from 01 through 99. Expansion is literal, single-pass, and case-sensitive; an unknown, repeated where disallowed, unexpanded, path-separator-bearing value, or surviving angle bracket fails before reservation
privateWritePolicy.eventRule: runId equals verificationRunReceiptPolicy.runId. allowedPaths is ordinal path-sorted and exact-key typed. events use contiguous non-boolean integer sequence values starting at 1; action/nullability is exact: CREATE has null oldPath/before identity/hash, DELETE has null after identity/hash, WRITE has null oldPath and both sides, and RENAME has distinct path/oldPath plus both sides. Paths are canonical repository-relative forward-slash text; file identities are lowercase fixed-width or null and hashes lowercase SHA-256 or null. beforeSha256/afterSha256 canonically hash the exact complete allowed-scope inventories, not event prose
privateWritePolicy.reservationRule: reservedHarnessRelativePaths and reservedHarnessPathTemplates are specifications, never runtime wildcard grants. Each transaction expands only its applicable templates into a finite ordinal exact allowedPaths list: an ordinary verification run expands ordinary <phase>/runs templates; a bootstrap verification run expands only bootstrap/attempts/<attempt-id>/<phase>/runs templates for check or independent-review; the bootstrap owner driver reserves each fixed attempt-level file immediately before its named journal transition; and bootstrap/bootstrap-foundation.json is reserved only for the one terminal publication after PARKED. Expansion uses only the selected dispatch phase, validated fresh runId, actual 1-based command/step counts, and where required the validated attemptId; every applicable placeholder is replaced and every inapplicable template is absent. All exact files under the own work-item log are created/opened by the harness before child launch with no-share-write/delete handles or an exclusively held parent; owner-only bootstrap transaction files have no child launch and remain exclusively held through atomic publication and re-read. They are writer=harness and can never be created, replaced, renamed, deleted, or written by the worker process. The append-only bootstrap journal alone admits atomic append records under its state rule. Worker artifacts require separate exact writer=worker-process rows and may not contain a reserved concrete prefix
privateWritePolicy.selfReferenceRule: the three exact postWindowReceiptNames in the selected run directory are pre-reserved with exclusive no-share-write/delete handles before child launch and any child access fails. They are deliberately excluded from beforeSha256/afterSha256 and events because they are serialized only after Job drain and final monitored inventories: first private-write-audit, then worktree-write-audit, then verification-run-receipt, each by atomic owner-harness replacement while the parent remains exclusively held. All other allowed output files, including streams and toolchain manifests/attestations, are inside the monitored inventory. No other self-exclusion or post-window child/worker write is legal, avoiding a self-hash cycle without opening an audit gap
privateWritePolicy.rule: before launch, derive an ordinal finite allowlist containing reserved harness paths, exact worker artifact files/directories declared by that row, and game/.godot/ only for rotwk-gate-v1; a broad own-log directory grant is forbidden. Inventory bounded scopes, then monitor workspace/logs, workspace/retail-work, workspace/content-packs, and game/.godot from before process creation through complete Job drain using Windows change notifications. Every event outside its exact writer/path authorization, another work-item log, cache/bytecode node, watcher overflow/error, cap breach, receipt substitution, or before/after protected-state drift fails
privateWritePolicy.trustLimit: this detects cooperative and ordinary descendant writes but is not a kernel sandbox; the lane must state that limit and may not infer arbitrary-filesystem non-interference

worktreeWritePolicy.modeRule: runId equals verificationRunReceiptPolicy.runId. worker-lane-v1 and bootstrap-candidate-v1 are verification of already-authored bytes: assignmentDigest follows dispatch and allowedTrackedPaths is empty so owned/candidate checkers, tests, imports, and data cannot self-substitute even temporarily. canonical-main-readonly-v1 has null assignmentDigest and empty allowedTrackedPaths; canonical-main-completion-v1 also has empty allowedTrackedPaths and has non-null assignmentDigest exactly when completing lane-v1, otherwise null; canonical-main-materialization-v1 has null assignmentDigest and allowedTrackedPaths exactly ['config/repository-boundaries.json','orchestration/feature-lane-plan.json','orchestration/work-items.json'] in ordinal order, but only the owner harness may mutate them post-Job under trackedWorktreeBindingPolicy. authorityRevision and repositoryBindingSha256 always equal the held mode binding. No other main mutation uses this receipt mode
worktreeWritePolicy.rule: monitor the complete bound lane or canonical-main worktree except the separately bound Git administrative directory from before child creation through Job drain and any final owner CAS. Worker descendants always have zero tracked-write authority; only the canonical-main-materialization owner harness may produce events at ordinal-exact allowedTrackedPaths after Job drain. Authorization never casefolds, and casefold is used only to reject collisions. Event sequence/action/path/oldPath nullability follows privateWritePolicy, rename detection is disabled for semantic tree deltas, both rename endpoints are checked, every vanished base path needs exact deletion authorization, and any cache/bytecode, unallowed, case-only, restored-after-write, overflow, or watcher error fails. Non-materialization modes require zero tracked events and identical before/after digest. Materialization additionally requires one isolated-index owner commit whose first-parent delta is exactly allowedTrackedPaths. Exact NUL-delimited raw HEAD/index/worktree/ignored inventories before and after produce the two canonical digests and must satisfy repositoryBindingPolicy.worktreeClosureRule and trackedWorktreeBindingPolicy

verificationCommandPolicy.toolchainAttestationRule: every profile yields one exact openbfme.toolchain-attestation schemaVersion 1 receipt whose attestationMode equals the selected profile. Every process is created under toolchainDeliveryRule with PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_HANDLE_LIST containing exactly NUL-read stdin plus stdout/stderr pipe write handles, and wrapper mode alone adds the dedicated attestation-pipe write handle. In wrapper mode the trusted bound wrapper emits the payload only over that dedicated pipe and the harness serializes it; in harness mode the harness derives and serializes it from held bindings plus the observed Job process image identities without a wrapper payload. tools is the ordinal role-sorted exact identity set containing the direct role and every auxiliary role actually invoked, each equal to the binding manifest. The harness validates work item, runId, phase, commandIndex, stepIndex, profile/mode, step and manifest digests, required/allowed roles, executable/runtime identities, and PASS before the step can satisfy evidence. The step receipt's toolchainAttestation is null only when the selected mode could not produce an authentic payload under verificationRunReceiptPolicy; a command PASS always has one. An undeclared descendant, absent/extra/stale/replayed payload, cross-command collision, wrong emitter mode, filesystem emission by a wrapper, drift, FAIL, or SKIP fails closed

featureLanePolicy.planEncodingRule: UTF-8 without BOM, ASCII content, LF line endings, terminal LF, two-space JSON indentation, and recursively ordinal-lexically sorted keys for every object including nested full work items while arrays retain their policy-declared semantic order; planSha256 is the lowercase SHA-256 of the exact raw bytes
featureLanePolicy.planOrderingRule: inputArtifacts sort by producerWorkItemId then path; trackedInputs sort by path; requirements, objectives, prerequisiteSlices, children, envelopes, and rollups sort by their primary ID; every nested ID/path set is unique ordinal case-sensitive sorted except requiredLevels and structured command steps, whose declared array order is semantic. requiredOutputDimensions is an exact six-key object whose semantic dimension order is evidenceDimensionPolicy.dimensionKeys, while planEncodingRule necessarily serializes its object keys ordinal-lexically; raw object member order never carries authority
featureLanePolicy.targetBindingRule: target is semantically byte-for-byte equal after strict JSON parse to the complete top-level ledger target object read from planningInputRevision; no projection, override, default, or current-main substitution is legal. The identical target object is copied into every generated assignment slice and rederived with its authority slice before every generated-lane check and handoff
featureLanePolicy.planAvailabilityRule: before materialization acceptedPlanArtifact is absent and every envelopeCompletion/generatedLane is absent or null as required; the accepted tracked plan permanently retains null in every nested planned generatedLane.planSha256 and envelopeCompletion.planSha256 field, and planSha256 is the raw SHA-256 of exactly those non-self-referential tracked bytes. Materialization injects that digest only into the corresponding materialized ledger work-item fields, never back into the tracked plan; thereafter the tracked artifact is mandatory, its raw digest matches, and every materialized ledger reference equals it
featureLanePolicy.materializationRule: the integration owner alone runs tools/plan-feature-lanes.py materialize/resume from a clean fresh main under the allocation lock; it rehashes every actual sealed/tracked input, validates the byte-identical private proposal, builds exactly acceptedPlanArtifact, orchestration/work-items.json, and config/repository-boundaries.json in an isolated Git index, inspects the exact diff, compare-and-swap installs one commit, and writes a typed private receipt; that three-path commit leaves P0-LANES-001 in verification, a distinct reviewer audits the exact commit/receipt, and only a later owner ledger-only direct-child acceptance transition may attach completionReceipt and mark it complete; interruption is resumable and never overwrites different bytes
featureLanePolicy.generatedAssignmentSliceRule: a generated assignment packet contains the exact requiredGeneratedAssignmentSliceKeys projection: full pins, parent, objective, complete planned child, exact requirements, and every relevant frozen prerequisite slice; slice raw SHA-256 and accepted plan raw SHA-256 are assignment-bound and recomputed before every check and handoff
featureLanePolicy.plannerRevisionRule: planningInputRevision is the one frozen Git tree named by every trackedInputs row; plannerPinRevision is its direct child and changes only policy-declared input pins plus the planner blocked-to-pending transition; plannerAssignmentRevision is the direct child allocator transition; plannerImplementationRevision is the distinct single reviewed worker commit, descends from assignment, is an ancestor of current main, and equals the typed planner completion implementationRevision; stale ancestors, self-referential pins, or substituted revisions block
featureLanePolicy.privateInputVerificationRule: owner proposal/materialization requires every sealed input file to exist and match its accepted producer implementation revision/path/raw SHA-256 and every tracked input to match planningInputRevision bytes; fresh-clone validation rechecks the tracked accepted plan, Git-addressed inputs and prerequisite rows, completion receipts, and recorded digests without pretending absent private bytes were re-read
featureLanePolicy.artifactDigestRule: completionReceipt.artifactDigests is an ordinal path-sorted non-empty array of unique exact requiredArtifactDigestKeys objects; path is one portable repository/workspace-relative literal file and sha256 is the lowercase SHA-256 of its raw bytes
featureLanePolicy.requirementIdentityEncoding: exact required identity and source-locator key order, canonical ASCII compact JSON with no insignificant whitespace and terminal LF, lowercase SHA-256; textual retail paths, names, decoded values, excerpts, or free-form prose are forbidden
featureLanePolicy.objectiveIdentityEncoding: exact required key order, canonical ASCII compact JSON with terminal LF and lowercase SHA-256; objectiveKind is a bounded lowercase token and objectiveKeySha256 is a lowercase digest
featureLanePolicy.childIdCollisionRule: a duplicate derived child ID, including a truncated-digest collision, blocks the plan
featureLanePolicy.identifierNamespaceRule: requirement IDs and work-item IDs are typed disjoint alphabets; a requirement ID is never resolved as a dependency or work-item identity

routingAuthority.rule: P0-LANES recomputes requirementId/objectiveId from exact sanitized identities, then copies every remaining typed row field verbatim; routingRuleId equals the exact terminal envelope ID, the dimension map has no default, and any missing, multi-envelope, unknown, identity-mismatched, raw-retail, private-path, or unowned mapping blocks

featureLanePolicy.batchingRule: group only identical terminal envelope, objective identity, requiredLevels, exact output-dimension map, and structured verification command; within each group sort requirements by ID and place each into the earliest existing batch whose requirement count, mutable-path union, and high-conflict union remain within caps, otherwise create the next batch; reject any plan not equal to this ordinal first-fit partition
featureLanePolicy.inputBindingRule: null pins are legal only while P0-LANES-001 is blocked; before the surgical planner-pin transition every producer is complete with typed completionReceipt, and each sealed pin equals its implementationRevision plus unique artifact digest; every tracked input points to planningInputRevision raw bytes; the accepted plan repeats all pins, and any missing, extra, stale, self-referential, mismatched, unaccepted-producer, or machine-absolute input blocks
featureLanePolicy.generatedLanePresenceRule: generatedLane is absent on ordinary worker lanes and is an exact requiredGeneratedLaneKeys object only on planner-generated children
featureLanePolicy.childPathCapRule: before allocation a generated child has at most maxMutableCandidatePathsPerChild exact mutable candidate paths; while active ownedPaths equals that mutable set and has at most maxOwnedPathsPerChild paths
